Theme

School & learning

professor noun

also professors, lecturer, university teacher, academic (a university teacher), academics

classical

Quint. 1.9.3: cōnsummātīs professōribus
Suet. Tib. 11.3: scholās et audītōria professōrum
Traupman 365
M-O s.v. professor

professor, professōris m.

noun, third declension

a professor, a public teacher

From profitērī, to declare publicly, and so to teach a subject in public; Lewis & Short: post-Augustan, a public teacher of any art (Celsus, Quintilian, Suetonius).

Other words

  • doctor, doctōris m. — a teacher; in the universities, a doctor

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.23 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. professor

    Classically any teacher; in the universities, the holder of a doctorate (Morgan–Owens).

Examples

  • cum circā scholās et audītōria professōrum assiduus esset

    since he was always about the lectures and lecture halls of the professorsSuet. Tib. 11.3

  • quod opus etiam cōnsummātīs professōribus difficile quī commodē tractāverit, cuicumque discendō sufficiet

    anyone who handles this task well, hard even for accomplished professors, will be equal to any learningQuint. 1.9.3

See also teacher, university, lecture, student, college, academic.
